main_notes.title: 5G, IoT, and VoIP in Smart Devices
Enhances clarity and reduces delay in VoIP calls
Everyday devices connected to the internet
Can make or receive VoIP calls
Devices in homes and workplaces can automatically connect for communication

key_terms.definition: A fifth-generation mobile network technology that offers high-speed internet, low latency, and increased capacity.
A system of interconnected devices, vehicles, home appliances, and other items embedded with electronics, software, sensors, and network connectivity to exchange data and perform tasks automatically.
A method of making telephone calls using a broadband internet connection instead of a traditional phone line.

examples: Your smart fridge calling you when it detects that the milk level is low.
Smart speakers scheduling a video call with your colleagues during a work meeting.
Wearable devices automatically sending reminders to take medication or attend scheduled appointments.
connections: 5G and IoT are closely related as both technologies enable seamless communication and data exchange among smart devices.
VoIP integrates well with 5G and IoT, enhancing the capabilities of smart devices by providing clear voice calls over the internet.
Smart homes and offices benefit from these technologies through automated scheduling, reminders, and improved communication.
questions: How does 5G improve the quality of VoIP calls compared to previous generations of mobile networks?
What are some potential applications of IoT in smart devices for personal and professional use beyond making and receiving VoIP calls?
In what ways can the integration of 5G, IoT, and VoIP contribute to the development of smart homes and offices?
